candidates.label: Cyprus (Roman province, label point)
candidates.support: Cyprus's identity and extent as the Roman province covering the whole island are undisputed; the coordinate is Wikidata's representative point for the province.

summary.text: Cyprus was a senatorial province covering the whole island, governed by a proconsul from Paphos. Barnabas, Paul's companion on the first missionary journey, was a Levite from Cyprus; Acts records that the two preached across the island, from Salamis to Paphos, where the proconsul Sergius Paulus believed.

history.text: Rome annexed Cyprus in 58 BC. In Augustus's 27 BC settlement it was at first retained under his own authority, together with Syria and Cilicia, per Cassius Dio's account, before being given to the Senate as a separate province in 22 BC; from then it was a senatorial province governed by a proconsul, matching the title Acts gives Sergius Paulus, an arrangement in force at AD 50.
